A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same research work. All 27 pages of each, including Appendices A–D, equations, figures, and tables, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic regression, colored-MNIST, Cityscapes, and COCO experiments in Section 4 and Appendix D, including numerical results and channel reconstructions.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in Section 4 and Appendix D, including Tables 2–8 and Figure 10.

M1.justification: The three-channel codec, conditional entropy models, common-representation matching procedure, and training objectives in Sections 3.2–3.3 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use synthetic regression, colored-MNIST digit/color classification under the same three PMFs, Cityscapes segmentation/depth estimation, and COCO 2017 object/keypoint detection.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across the corresponding experiments, including Combined, Separated, Joint, and Independent codecs. Section 4.2's revised 'model trained on the Independent PMF' wording identifies an existing condition in Figure 4 and Table 6, rather than changing a baseline.

E3.justification: Table 1 and Appendix D retain identical training settings, preprocessing, model dimensions, parameter sweeps, validation procedures, and rate/distortion metrics.

E4.justification: The architecture ablations and transmit–receive tradeoff analyses in Figures 3 and 9, PMF edge cases in Figure 4, and channel-reconstruction analysis in Figure 10 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repeat counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 2–8, the experimental curves, and channel reconstructions are identical. Both conclusions report the same average -81.58% transmit BD-rate advantage. The Section 4.2 wording clarification does not change the findings already shown in Figure 4 and Table 6.

T1.justification: Appendix C corrects the coefficient in Theorem 3, Equation 92, from undefined K to the stipulated Lipschitz constant µ, aligning the stated bound with its existing proof in Equation 94. This is a localized theorem-statement correction; the assumptions and proof are unchanged. Added grouping braces in Equations 76–77 do not change their mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: lossy-common-information bounds, a learnable Gray–Wyner codec, transmit–receive tradeoff optimization, and improved efficiency over independent coding.

C2.justification: The explanations of common-channel behavior, separability limitations, auxiliary-loss restrictions, and extension beyond two tasks are unchanged. Section 4.2 clarifies which PMF-trained model exhibits the existing observation without changing its explanation.

D1.justification: Implementation descriptions, training details, Table 1, Appendix D, and the code-availability statement are unchanged. The added funding acknowledgment supplies no new technical or resource-access information.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the cited works are unchanged. References displaced onto later pages by the acknowledgment are retained, with no change in research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 adds an Intel Labs/NSERC acknowledgment, changes the conference header from 'Accepted' to 'Published,' clarifies the method-versus-PMF wording in Section 4.2, and makes limited equation notation and punctuation edits. The scientific narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: The acknowledgment reflows the bibliography across pages 11–13 and shifts the opening of Appendix A. Local text and equation spacing also changes. All figures and tables retain their displays, captions, and locations.

improvement.justification: v2 removes ambiguity between the Independent codec and the model trained on the Independent PMF in Section 4.2, and corrects Equation 92 to match its stated assumption and existing proof. These localized clarity and consistency improvements, together with funding disclosure, modestly improve the paper while leaving its methods, empirical evidence, and broader conclusions unchanged.
